explanation: A number base tells how many digits a counting system uses before carrying over. Base 10 (decimal) uses digits 0–9. Base 2 (binary) uses only 0 and 1. The subscript shows the base, e.g. 1011₂. Each position stands for a power of the base: in binary the places from the right are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and so on. To convert TO base 10, multiply each digit by its place value and add. To convert FROM base 10, divide repeatedly by the new base and read the remainders upward.
key_points: The subscript shows the base: 1011₂ is binary, 45₁₀ is decimal.
To base 10: multiply digits by place values and add.
From base 10: divide repeatedly, read remainders upward.
objectives: Explain what a number base is.
Convert numbers between base 10 and base 2.
Read and write numbers with base subscripts.
subject: Mathematics
title: Number Bases

steps: Add the two equations: (2x + y) + (x − y) = 7 + 2.

examples.title: Solve 2x + y = 7 and x − y = 2

steps: Subtract the second equation from the first: (3x + 2y) − (x + 2y) = 12 − 8.
examples.title: Solve 3x + 2y = 12 and x + 2y = 8

explanation: Simultaneous equations are two equations that must be true at the same time, e.g. 2x + y = 7 and x − y = 2. The pair (x, y) that satisfies both is the solution. The elimination method removes one unknown: add or subtract the equations so that one variable cancels out, then solve for the other. Use it when one variable has the same (or opposite) coefficient in both equations, like +y and −y above. After finding one value, substitute it into either equation to find the other, then check your answer in both equations.
key_points: Simultaneous equations share one solution pair (x, y).
Elimination: add or subtract to cancel one variable.
Substitute the found value into either equation for the other.
Always check the answer in BOTH equations.
objectives: Solve pairs of equations by elimination.
Verify a solution in both equations.

title: Algebra: Simultaneous Equations

steps: Angles in a triangle add to 180°.
examples.title: Find the third angle of a triangle with 60° and 70°

explanation: An angle measures turning between two lines meeting at a point, measured in degrees (°). An acute angle is less than 90°, a right angle is exactly 90°, an obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°, and angles on a straight line add up to 180°. A triangle has three sides and three angles, and its three interior angles ALWAYS add up to 180° — this is the single most useful fact for WAEC/NECO angle problems. If you know two angles of a triangle, subtract their sum from 180° to find the third.
key_points: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.
Interior angles of ANY triangle sum to 180°.
Third angle = 180° − (sum of the other two).
objectives: Classify acute, right and obtuse angles.
Find a missing angle using the triangle 180° rule.
